rationale: The refresher — the half DGH-018 and the approved 5a33a174 round both named as the stated unbuilt residual, ordered built by the owner in the same message as the SQL apply. It closes the gap between the token's life (42 days served) and the presign's 7-day SigV4 ceiling: without it every /d/ link quietly enters the honest-but-unwanted 'being refreshed' state a week after its last stamp and recovery is a manual operator act. With it, a 6h schedule re-stamps anything dying within 48h, so a customer should never see the stale page in normal operation — and the customer-facing backstop (honest page + persisted ZIP_LINK_STALE row) stays armed for the abnormal case. The shape reuses everything proven: the pre_query-driven scheduler idiom, 459's spawn->call pair (zip-deliverer stays the ONLY presign minter, bugs_open/245 untouched), and one new pure-DB action whose WHERE is the entire safety: a refresh can never resurrect a REVOKED link or extend an EXPIRED token's closed window — both predicates mutation-relevant and pinned by regex in the test. Zero rows updated is a WARN not an error, deliberately: the token can legitimately expire between pre_query and dispatch, and failing the run would make a benign race read as a broken refresher at every occurrence. INHERITED AND STATED: the spawn->call handshake fails ~half the time fleet-wide; a FAILED run self-heals at the next tick because the pre_query re-selects anything still unstamped, and the seed header says never to cancel the failing row pre-diagnosis. The honest health check is the OUTCOME query in the seed header (live tokens with dead presigns, want 0), not run status.

Seed verify block asserts the agent active, the schedule enabled and targeted, and the pre_query still carrying its three protective predicates.

edits.rationale: Pure DB; the presign arrives from zip-deliverer via the workflow, so no credentials move. The WHERE is the safety and each predicate is a named resurrection if dropped: purpose (a confirm token must never grow a URL), revoked_at IS NULL (an operator-killed link must stay dead), expires_at > now (refreshing inside an expired token quietly extends a window the handover stamp closed). Empty presign refused before any DB touch — writing '' would turn every live token stale at once, the link-born-broken shape MintZipToken refuses at mint. Zero rows = WARN: benign pre_query-to-dispatch race, not a failure.
edits.sketch:
res, err := params.DB.ExecContext(ctx, `
		UPDATE customer_access_tokens
		   SET stored_url            = $2,
		       stored_url_expires_at = $3
		 WHERE site_id    = $1
		   AND purpose    = 'zip_download'
		   AND revoked_at IS NULL
		   AND expires_at > $4
	`, siteID, presignedURL, now.Add(time.Duration(mins)*time.Minute), now)
	n, _ := res.RowsAffected()
	if n == 0 {
		logger.Warn("zip link refresh matched no live tokens (benign if the token expired since the pre_query...)")
	}

The schedule's pre_query mirrors the action's predicates PLUS `stored_url_expires_at IS NULL OR < now()+48h` — NULL matters: a token minted before its presign was stored (or by the operator recovery recipe without one) must be selected, not invisible. 6h cadence against a 48h window = ~8 chances before a customer could see staleness. Zero live tokens today = zero dispatches. _HOLD because it names refresh_zip_link (image before seeds; same roll as 651's actions). edits.sketch:
INSERT INTO scheduled_tasks (name, ..., pre_query, enabled)
SELECT 'zip-link-refresh', ..., 21600, 'zip-link-refresher', ...,
  $Q$SELECT DISTINCT t.site_id::text AS site_id, s.domain
       FROM customer_access_tokens t JOIN sites s ON s.id = t.site_id
      WHERE t.purpose = 'zip_download'
        AND t.revoked_at IS NULL
        AND t.expires_at > now()
        AND (t.stored_url_expires_at IS NULL
             OR t.stored_url_expires_at < now() + interval '48 hours')$Q$,
  true
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM scheduled_tasks WHERE name = 'zip-link-refresh');

THE GAP BEING CLOSED, measured 2026-08-20 at the live bucket (handover.go's header): X-Amz-Expires=604801 -> 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch, exact to the second — the presign ceiling is real, enforced by the store not the SDK, and its error reads as broken credentials, which is why /d/ never redirects to a stale URL and why the refresher must run BEFORE expiry rather than react after.

THE SCHEDULER IDIOM, copied not invented: scheduled_tasks.pre_query rows drive per-row dispatch (the intent-collection row is the worked example read before writing this one: SELECT site_id, domain FROM sites WHERE ...). The refresher's pre_query returns the same (site_id, domain) shape.

THE SPAWN->CALL PAIR, copied from 459 verbatim including its load-bearing comment about '?'-suffixed optional mappings; this workflow maps only the required `domain`. INHERITED RISK STATED: spawn->call fails ~half the time fleet-wide (2 COMPLETED / 2 FAILED all-history at the time of that memory) — a FAILED refresher run self-heals at the next 6h tick because the pre_query re-selects anything still unstamped; the seed header says never to cancel the failing row pre-diagnosis and gives the OUTCOME health query (live tokens with dead presigns, want 0) as the honest meter, not run status.

The zero-rows and empty-presign behaviours each have a dedicated test; the empty-presign test documents the two-doors-in-series finding (extraction refuses resolved-empty before the in-action guard can) rather than pretending the inner guard fired.
